title: Artemis-Switch, PC streaming on a Switch

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Imagine playing your PC's Steam Big Picture on a Nintendo Switch, with a live panel showing how the stream is doing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. It's Antoine's maintained fork of Moonlight-Switch, built for Apollo hosts, the Sunshine family of streaming servers. You stream a Windows or Linux PC, and the Switch decodes the video and acts as the screen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What's the app like to use?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It has two in-app menus while you stream. Quick has host shortcuts, keyboard presets and Apollo scripts. Performance shows live bitrate and latency stats, so you can see how the connection feels.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: C plus plus homebrew, from the devkitA64 and libnx lineage that Moonlight-Switch uses, with Apollo and Sunshine pairing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You install the dot nro file and pair with an Apollo host on your home network. The README covers the build prerequisites. The blog article on handheld streaming has screenshots of both menus.
